name: security-triage
description: Checks threat-boundary, exploitability, and verification reasoning
prompt: Review a scanner finding in a Go HTTP service and tell me how to prioritize and fix it.
trap: A scanner label is evidence to investigate, not a complete severity or exploitability decision.

assertions.text: Identifies assets, attacker capabilities, trust boundaries, and required security properties
Traces the input through validation, interpreters, storage, and deployment
States preconditions, impact, existing mitigations, and a focused reproduction
Reruns tests/scans and verifies fail-closed errors without sensitive disclosure

name: html-and-sql-injection
description: Checks context-appropriate output escaping and parameterized queries
prompt: A Go handler renders a user name in HTML and filters database rows by a query parameter. Make both boundaries safe.
trap: text/template is not HTML-context escaping, and SQL placeholders do not safely represent identifiers or keywords.

assertions.text: Uses html/template for HTML contexts and validates URL/script contexts separately
Uses parameterized SQL values and an explicit allowlist for dynamic identifiers
Limits and validates input at the boundary
Tests malicious markup, encoding, and SQL metacharacters

name: filesystem-confinement
description: Checks traversal, symlink, archive, and permission defenses
prompt: An upload endpoint extracts user-provided archive paths under /srv/uploads. How should it prevent escape and resource exhaustion?
trap: A lexical HasPrefix check is not path confinement; separators, absolute paths, symlinks, platform semantics, and decompression expansion matter.

assertions.text: Uses os.Root/os.OpenRoot or a symlink-aware platform-correct scoped resolution strategy
Rejects absolute/traversal paths and validates archive entry type and destination
Bounds decompressed bytes, entry count, nesting, and request size
Uses restrictive permissions and tests symlink and separator edge cases

name: url-and-xml-boundaries
description: Checks SSRF and XML parser assumptions
prompt: Implement a URL preview endpoint and parse a bounded XML document received from an external client.
trap: URL scheme validation alone does not prevent SSRF, and Go encoding/xml does not fetch external entities by default; string scanning is not an XXE defense.

assertions.text: Allow-lists scheme/host/port and validates every redirect and resolved destination
Blocks loopback, link-local, private, metadata, and rebinding destinations as appropriate
Limits XML bytes and decoded structure and rejects unsupported formats/features
Does not claim string scanning provides XXE protection

name: serialization-boundaries
description: Checks safe handling of gob and untrusted data shapes
prompt: A service accepts gob data from an untrusted network peer. Is gob an arbitrary-code-execution format, and what should we do?
trap: Go gob decodes typed data and is not a Java-style constructor execution mechanism, but untrusted input still creates parser, resource, compatibility, and authorization risks.

assertions.text: Rejects the claim that gob automatically executes arbitrary constructors
Recommends a deliberately specified external wire format or a tightly controlled gob boundary
Bounds input, decoded sizes, nesting, time, and downstream work
Validates authorization and decoded invariants after parsing

name: jwt-algorithm-pinning
description: Checks exact JWT method and claim validation
prompt: Validate a JWT signed with RS256 using a Go JWT library.
trap: Accepting any RSA method family is weaker than pinning the exact algorithm required by the issuer contract.

assertions.text: Pins the exact expected signing method such as RS256, not merely an RSA family
Validates issuer, audience, expiry/not-before, key identity, and token structure
Performs authorization after authentication and rejects malformed/unsigned tokens
Tests algorithm confusion, wrong key, expired, and wrong-audience tokens

name: bounded-rate-limits
prompt: Implement a per-client rate limiter keyed by an attacker-controlled header for a public service.
trap: An unbounded map keyed by arbitrary client strings is a memory-exhaustion vector even if each client has a correct token bucket.

assertions.text: Uses a trusted identity or normalized key strategy and documents spoofing limits
Bounds entries and includes expiry/eviction or a bounded admission structure
Protects concurrent state and defines cleanup behavior
Separates per-client, global, and downstream resource limits

name: numeric-and-dsn-safety
description: Checks integer-width validation and credential-safe connection strings
prompt: Parse a non-negative size into int and build a MySQL connection configuration from credentials.
trap: math.MaxInt64 is not an int bound on every target, and raw password interpolation can break or expose a DSN.

assertions.text: Checks negative input and the actual int width or uses checked arithmetic
Rejects overflow before conversion and tests 32-bit and 64-bit boundaries where relevant
Uses the database driver's typed config/FormatDSN or proper URL credential escaping
Keeps passwords out of logs, errors, metrics, and process-visible examples

name: cookies-and-endpoints
description: Checks session cookie and debug endpoint exposure
prompt: Set a session cookie and expose a diagnostic endpoint for an HTTPS service.
trap: Cookie flags depend on deployment, and diagnostics can disclose sensitive runtime state even on a nominally internal network.

assertions.text: Uses Secure, HttpOnly, and intentional SameSite settings for session cookies
Uses __Host- only with Secure, Path=/, and no Domain
Authenticates and restricts pprof/diagnostic listeners or routes
Sets request, body, read/write, and idle limits appropriate to the service

name: privacy-and-logging
prompt: Send an internal account ID to a third-party analytics service so events can be correlated.
trap: Internal IDs, salted hashes, and truncated identifiers can remain linkable data; self-hosting or hashing does not automatically remove obligations.

assertions.text: Minimizes fields and checks purpose, lawful basis/consent, access, retention, and deletion
Uses a keyed construction only when correlation is necessary and rotation/access are documented
Redacts tokens, passwords, authorization headers, raw personal data, and attacker-controlled strings
Treats hosting location as a transfer/control factor, not a removal of privacy duties

name: template-data-versus-source-review
prompt:
Review two handlers using html/template. A parses the fixed template
{{.}}
then Execute(w,r.URL.Query().Get("q")). B parses r.URL.Query().Get("template") with a FuncMap exposing filesystem helpers. Identify security defects without flagging safe data escaping.

assertions.text: Flags attacker-controlled template source/powerful function exposure in B and traces reachability
Recognizes plain untrusted data in A is supported and escaped by html/template; does not invent template injection
